body:
PR #2002 proves the STORY-1352 guard you merged cannot see the drift it was built for — two contract commands did not exist

Open on bug-1289, rebased onto current main. No verdict from me, I wrote the prompt. The conformance work is routine; this mail is about what it found on the way.

THE FINDING. The lane audited all twelve contract surfaces EMPIRICALLY — built the binary and ran each one — rather than reading the manifest. Two commands the contract advertises did not exist at all:

  aida queue progress --json   -> clap: unexpected argument '--json'
  aida findings list --json    -> clap: unexpected argument '--json'

Both are named in the manifest and in docs/monitor-contract.md. A consumer following the contract hits a hard parse error.

WHY THE GUARD MISSED IT, and I verified this in the merged code rather than inferring it. docs/monitor-contract-fixtures/verify.py runs exactly one AIDA command — `aida contract --json`, the manifest itself — plus `git cat-file` and `git ls-tree` for the base-ref comparison. It never invokes a single surface the contract describes. So it validates hand-authored fixtures against a hand-authored manifest, and the two agreed perfectly while two of the commands they described were unrunnable.

That is the round-1 finding on STORY-1352 restated by events: the mechanism built to detect silent drift has the silent-drift flaw in it. You checked the enforcement rather than the prose when you merged #1987, which was the right instinct — the enforcement is real, it just validates the wrong pair. A fixture cannot disagree with a manifest that was written from it.

I am NOT proposing you unwind anything. #1987's version bump enforcement is genuinely useful and the lane has now made the contract true by implementing both missing commands. What is left is that the guard still cannot tell. Adding "invoke each covered command and parse its output" to verify.py is a small change to a file that already imports subprocess, and it converts the contract from documentation into a checked interface. Your call whether that belongs on STORY-1352 as a follow-up or on the follow-up you already recorded there about the docs path filter — they are the same file and arguably the same fix.

ONE MORE THING WORTH THE READER'S EYE. `aida usage` needed the fix in TWO places, and the one that mattered was the live git-canonical dispatch in git_backend_cmd.rs, not the legacy arm in lib.rs. A lane reading code alone would plausibly have patched the dead path, seen the tests pass, and shipped a fix that did nothing. It found the right one by running the binary. That is an argument for empirical audits over code reading that I would not have made this strongly yesterday.

BUG-1291 ROUND 2 BRIEFED, three findings, all restated as numbered requirements with their own acceptance — I am applying the STORY-1350 lesson that advisory framing gets skipped. Finding 1 is "the test asserts a mock hook was invoked, never exercises RealPhaseDriver" — the eighth instance of the acceptance-names-a-boundary-implementation-tests-below-it class, which is precisely what TASK-1290 is being built to catch right now. Finding 2 is a handoff that reports Filed while discarding queue-add failures, which recreates the ownerless condition this spec exists to fix and adds a false record on top. Finding 3 is a sweep predicate counting only Approved as a verdict, so a RequestChanges PR reads as ownerless and gets re-driven on work a reviewer already refused.

Lanes: BUG-1289 delivered, TASK-1290 running. I hold at two.
